title: Kubernetes Pod Scheduling Quick Revision
summary: Quick revision notes on how the Kubernetes scheduler places pods: nodeSelector, node and pod affinity, taints and tolerations, topology spread, and resource requests. Ends with a cheat sheet.

chapters.title: Scheduling Mental Model
points: Scheduler runs two phases per pod: filter (drop nodes that cannot fit) then score (rank survivors), then binds the pod to the top node
Pod stays Pending with a FailedScheduling event when no node passes filtering
Attraction tools pull pods toward nodes: nodeSelector, node affinity, pod affinity. Repulsion tools push away: taints, pod anti-affinity
Taints live on nodes and tolerations on pods; a toleration only permits a node, it never attracts the pod to it
Scheduling is decided once at placement; 'IgnoredDuringExecution' means later label changes do not evict running pods

chapters.title: nodeSelector and Node Affinity
points: nodeSelector: exact key=value label match in pod spec; multiple entries are ANDed; simplest hard constraint
Label a node with kubectl label node worker-1 disktype=ssd, then set spec.nodeSelector: {disktype: ssd}
requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution is a hard rule; preferredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution is a soft rule with weight 1-100 added to node score
Node affinity operators: In, NotIn, Exists, DoesNotExist, Gt, Lt; NotIn and DoesNotExist give node anti-affinity
Multiple nodeSelectorTerms are ORed, while matchExpressions inside one term are ANDed; if both nodeSelector and affinity are set, both must match

chapters.title: Pod Affinity and Anti-Affinity
points: Pod affinity places a pod in the same topology domain as pods matching a labelSelector; anti-affinity keeps it out of that domain
topologyKey is required and picks the domain: kubernetes.io/hostname = per node, topology.kubernetes.io/zone = per zone
Anti-affinity with required + hostname spreads replicas one per node; with 3 nodes, a 4th replica stays Pending
Use preferred anti-affinity (with weight) to spread replicas best effort without blocking scale-out
Pod affinity is costly at scale in large clusters, and the labelSelector must match the target pods' labels, not the pod's own namespace by default (set namespaces to widen it)

chapters.title: Taints, Tolerations and Effects
points: Taint a node: kubectl taint nodes node1 key=value:NoSchedule; remove it with a trailing minus: key=value:NoSchedule-
Toleration fields: key, operator (Equal or Exists), value, effect; operator Exists with no key tolerates every taint
NoSchedule blocks new pods without the toleration but leaves running pods alone; PreferNoSchedule is the soft version
NoExecute also evicts running pods that lack the toleration; tolerationSeconds delays eviction by that many seconds

Control plane nodes carry node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane:NoSchedule; node controller adds not-ready and unreachable NoExecute taints (default 300s toleration via DaemonSet-like injection into pods)

chapters.title: Topology Spread and Resource Requests
points: topologySpreadConstraints fields: maxSkew, topologyKey, whenUnsatisfiable (DoNotSchedule or ScheduleAnyway), labelSelector
maxSkew is the max allowed difference in matching pod count between the fullest and emptiest domain; maxSkew 1 across zones gives an even spread
Topology spread balances evenly across domains, whereas anti-affinity only allows at most one per domain; spread is the better choice for HA across zones
Scheduler fits pods using the sum of requests (not limits or live usage) against node allocatable; high requests cause Pending with 'Insufficient cpu/memory'
Requests also set QoS class: requests equal limits gives Guaranteed, requests below limits gives Burstable, none gives BestEffort (evicted first)

chapters.title: Scheduling Cheat Sheet
points: Debug a Pending pod: kubectl describe pod <name> and read the Events for FailedScheduling reasons
Inspect labels and taints: kubectl get nodes --show-labels; kubectl describe node <n> | grep -i taint
Which tool: pin to node type = nodeSelector or node affinity; co-locate or separate pods = pod affinity or anti-affinity; reserve nodes = taint plus toleration plus nodeSelector
Reserving dedicated nodes needs BOTH a taint (keeps others out) and node affinity or nodeSelector (pulls your pods in)
Quick effects table: NoSchedule = block new only; PreferNoSchedule = avoid if possible; NoExecute = block new and evict existing
